Other inputs return LANEC_OUT_OF_SCOPE with the image and I/O unchanged (suite di-refuse: 384 corrupted entry states; di-idle: 122 and di-nvdsp: 114 out-of-range COPINDEX/COPMPAC states, refused by the steps that index with them). On the C64, where each program links only the modules of one mission, di-transfer-c64 refuses 28 call chains, image and I/O unchanged, that end at an in-range point only an unlinked routine could continue; the host suite di-transfer, with every routine linked, compares those same chains. The round trips into the mark, sleep, idle and nvdsp modules run on the C64 in di-transfer-c64m (one program per module group and mission: mark with nvdsp, sleep with idle), which refuses 38 such chains the same way. The host suite di-transfer has no C64 program of its own (with the Luminary099 Executive linked the round trip does not fit one): 705 of its 934 branch arcs are taken by the other suites' C64 rows, and the other 229 are marked host-only in the C64 record: the Executive sources (executive.c, lm_exec_*, lm_basic_*, lm_admission_image.c, p66_native.c, which run on the C64 in Lane A's Executive milestones such as vice-lm-exec-jobs), the host runner's merged LM interbank and Executive site and table set-up, and agc_classify's +0/-0 returns, which these chains reach only inside the Executive.
supported_domain.hardware_side_effects: The file does channel I/O in two places: WITCHONE's WAND DSALMOUT writes channel 011 (clears bit 5, the KEY REL light), and OKTOPLAY/VACDSP's ROR SUPERBNK only read channel 07 into A to save the superbank with the bank. The channel 011 value is kept exactly in the carried I/O; lighting the DSKY lamp from it is the device adapter's job, as for the other Lane C modules.

Each entry returns EXEC_OUT_OF_SCOPE before any change for inputs outside its guard. The interpretive entries use the generated sane() (at NEWOPS of bank 37 with BANKSET, FB, SUPERBNK and INTBIT15 agreeing): an incoherent bank set, NEWJOB -0 or negative, FIXLOC not a VAC area, a nonzero word 7, an interrupt-enable value over 1, stray SUPERBNK bits or a word over 15 bits. P21VSAVE's DDV P21VEL (2102) also starts from edge operands in half its cases: MPAC 0, -0 or small, and P21VEL 0, -0, small, major part +-1 with a minor of either sign, 1/2, or a major part equal to MPAC's; edge_values gives the other operands edge vectors in a quarter of the cases.

A result the device record cannot carry, CHANLOAD's WRITE to a channel outside it, is refused the same way. On the C64, where each program links INTER-BANK and one module, pin-transfer-c64 refuses 1,179 call chains, image and I/O unchanged, that end where only an unlinked module, the display interface or the Executive could continue; pin-transfer, with every routine linked, compares those chains.

Basic (cm_powered_subs_basic): 3500, 3504 (after EXIT), 3530, 3536, 3546 (CD*TR*GS after CDULOGIC, COSINE and SINE), 3555 QUICTRIG, 3566, 3575 (after SPSIN, SPCOS), 3622, 3625, 3635, 3640, 3645, 3647 (after EXIT), 3627, 3642 (after MPACVBUF), 3676, 3714 (AX*SR*T after DMPSUB). Resume points start in the states the file's own runs leave there: TEM3 or ITEMP2 an angle offset 0, 2 or 4; DEXDEX +-1 to +-3, DEX1/DEX2 offsets, BUF 0 or 1; TEM2, ITEMP1 and RTNSAVER a return address (a TC in this file or a fixed address outside it); NBSM's S1 an erasable address of three angles. Each entry returns EXEC_OUT_OF_SCOPE before any change for inputs outside its guard. The interpretive entries use the generated sane() (at NEWOPS of the routine's bank with BANKSET, FB and INTBIT15 agreeing): an incoherent bank set, NEWJOB -0 or negative, FIXLOC not a VAC area, a nonzero word 7, an interrupt-enable value over 1, stray SUPERBNK bits or a word over 15 bits. The basic entries use the generated basic_sane(): FB not the routine's bank (23), an incoherent EB/BB, a nonzero word 7, an interrupt-enable value over 1, stray SUPERBNK bits or a word over 15 bits; NEWJOB and FIXLOC take any value. At the returns after SPSIN and SPCOS (3566, 3575) A takes values across its range, +-0 in about a fifth of the cases, so MP BIT14 runs with a +-0 multiplicand. SMCDURES (3742) and its DDV COSCDUZ (3751) also start from edge operands: DTHETASM zero or small (so the dividend is), MPAC 0, -0 or small, and COSCDUZ 0, -0, small, major part +-1 with a minor of either sign, 1/2, or a major part equal to the dividend's; with edge_values on the other operands, the shared DDV's zero-dividend, x/0, 0/0, equal-major and major-1 arcs all run (reviewer 1, #314).

The host suite di-transfer has no C64 program of its own (with the Luminary099 Executive linked the round trip does not fit one): 705 of its 934 branch arcs are taken by the other suites' C64 rows, and the other 229 are marked host-only in the C64 record: the Executive sources (executive.c, lm_exec_*, lm_basic_*, lm_admission_image.c, p66_native.c, which run on the C64 in Lane A's Executive milestones such as vice-lm-exec-jobs), the host runner's merged LM interbank and Executive site and table set-up, and agc_classify's +0/-0 returns, which these chains reach only inside the Executive.

RESUME, NOQRSM and NOQBRSM need BRUPT equal to the word before ZRUPT (fixed words read under the interrupted FB and the current SUPERBNK), which is what the interrupt stores and what any producer that resumes through this file leaves: the programs that rewrite BRUPT resume elsewhere (the LM DAP's SUPERJOB set-up through INTERRUPT_LEAD_INS' NOQBRSM, with BRUPT = SUPERJOB's TCF RATELOOP and ZRUPT = SUPERJOB +1, again the word before ZRUPT). WHIMPER (ALARM_AND_ABORT) and CONTABRT (P70-P71) also store BRUPT but execute their own RESUME instruction, outside this file. The comparison's refused cases are exactly those with BRUPT changed in one bit, which no producer reaches. Other inputs return EXEC_OUT_OF_SCOPE before any change.
supported_domain.hardware_side_effects: Channel values are kept exactly (WAND/WOR/RAND/WRITE results as yaAGC computes them); firing the jets from channels 5 and 6 and running the TIME6 counter from channel 13 bit 15 are device-adapter obligations.
